newsitem.title: HUNGARY: May milling wheat up, maize down in slow Budapest.
newsitem.headline: May milling wheat up, maize down in slow Budapest.

text.p: May milling wheat and maize futures went in opposite directions on Monday on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) amid disappointing turnover, traders said.
"Most players took a wait-and-see attitude on Monday after the last two weeks' speculation-driven price movements," said Imre Uzonyi of Swap Broker.
May milling wheat rose by the daily allowed 400-forint limit to end at 24,400 forints per tonne but only 30 contracts changed hands.
However, the rising trend was unlikely to hold, Uzonyi said.
"A sharp downward movement would start shortly, especially if there is another limit-up rise on Tuesday," he said.
August was the only other traded milling wheat maturity but it remained unchanged at 21,500 forints.
Untraded July rose 200 forints to end at 21,000.
May maturity maize was the most traded on Monday, accounting for 96 contracts of a total 163 contracts or 63.1 million forints grains futures turnover.
May maize ended at 17,350 forints, down 190.
